content: Lobelia erinus, commonly referred to by its English names such as Annual Lobelia, Edging Lobelia, Garden Lobelia, or Trailing Lobelia, is a cool-season annual plant. It is capable of thriving across USDA hardiness zones 2 through 11 and is available in several distinct varieties. Some of the more popular varieties include Riviera, Blue Moon, Fountain, and Cascade. This plant's flowers exhibit a preference for full shade conditions. For optimal growth in gardens, it is recommended to start the seeds indoors prior to the last frost of the season. Once the risk of frost has completely subsided, the seedlings can be transplanted outdoors. When fully mature, the flowers typically reach a height of approximately 6 inches. To ensure healthy growth, the plants should be spaced at intervals of 6 to 9 inches apart. The blooming period for Lobelia erinus extends from mid-summer to late fall. In certain regions, the flowers may continue to bloom into early winter.
